name: Rick Santorum

summary.text: Rick Santorum, then a Republican U.S. Senator from Pennsylvania, introduced S.786, the National Weather Services Duties Act of 2005, in April 2005. The bill would have barred the National Weather Service from providing products or services that the private sector provides, apart from severe-weather warnings and forecasts to protect life and property. It was referred to the Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee and did not become law.

sources.title: Reining In The National Weather Service

facts.claim: Santorum introduced S.786 in April 2005; it was referred to the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation on April 14, 2005.
facts.quote: under review by the Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation since 14 April 2005

facts.claim: The bill's text provided that the National Weather Service shall not provide, or assist other entities in providing, a service or product that the private sector provides, with an exception for severe weather forecasts and warnings to protect life and property.
facts.quote: The National Weather Service shall not provide, or assist other entities in providing, a service or product

sources.title: Reining In The National Weather Service

facts.claim: In floor remarks Santorum said the bill modernised the statutory description of the Weather Service's role to reflect a reality in which the NWS and the commercial weather industry both play important parts.
facts.quote: reflects today's reality in which the NWS and the commercial weather industry both play important parts

sources.title: Reining In The National Weather Service

facts.claim: Critics read the bill as curtailing perceived government competition with commercial weather services and expected it to end most public dissemination of NWS forecasts and data outside severe-weather alerts; the bill's wording was widely considered unclear.
